Classify candidate methylation links by stricter distance windows.  The main candidate tables include promoter, gene-body, and nearest-gene links within 100 kb. This script tests how much final-candidate support depends on the broad 100 kb window by summarizing promoter/gene-body and nested TSS distance windows for human CpG links and mouse DMR links.

First-pass target-gene analysis for GSE202938 TcMAC21 cerebellum RNA-seq.  The submitter-supplied normalized-count matrix uses identifiers like ``chr1.10263`` instead of gene symbols. This script first tests whether those identifiers can be treated as coordinate-like bins on the custom reference described by the paper (mouse mm39 plus human chr21). When that mapping is too uncertain, it writes an audit table and stops short of reporting gene-level effects.

Analyze Dp(10)2Yey hippocampus scRNA-seq target-gene expression from GSE214273.  The GEO supplementary file contains raw 10x-style Matrix Market files but no cell-type annotation table. This script therefore uses two conservative views: sample-level pseudobulk expression and per-sample target-gene detection fractions across all recovered cells.

Annotate candidate CpG-gene links with fetal brain Hi-C TAD support.  This is intentionally conservative. Won et al. GSE77565 provides processed CP/GZ TADs in hg19. The analysis asks whether DNMT3L-sensitive CpGs and the candidate gene TSS fall in the same fetal cortex TAD. Same-TAD support is not treated as a direct enhancer-promoter loop.

Integrate candidate-locus evidence for the DNMT3L mechanism question.  This script intentionally keeps three evidence layers separate: 1. candidate-linked methylation/expression evidence from existing gene/probe tables, 2. local fetal DS scATAC support from hg38 peak/window overlap, 3. context-level HOMER motif-family enrichment from altered-region sets.  The HOMER layer is not treated as exact motif-instance evidence at a candidate locus unless a separate motif-scanning step is performed.

Scan processed expression matrices for DNMT3/STAT target genes.  The script is intentionally format-tolerant: point it at a file or directory of tab/comma-delimited expression matrices and it will search likely annotation columns for target gene symbols or Ensembl IDs.

Collect Down syndrome/trisomy 21 brain-neural GEO candidates from NCBI.  The goal is broad recall, not final curation. The script queries NCBI GDS with multiple overlapping terms, de-duplicates GEO Series records, scores each record for brain/neural relevance, and writes compact TSV inventories for follow-up.

Compare DS/control target-gene expression across downloaded GEO datasets.  The broad cross-dataset view reports within-dataset, within-context case-control effects instead of pooling values across platforms. Fetal bulk GSE301886 and GSE305139 use precomputed edgeR count-based logFC values when available.

Compare DS brain methylation datasets with the DNMT3L-OE methylation signature.  This is a candidate-probe first pass.  The direct DNMT3L-overexpression anchor is GSE157078, called as EPIC candidate DMCs in results/human_candidate_dmrs/GSE157078_candidate_dmcs.tsv.  DS datasets are 450K-era arrays, so probe IDs provide the cleanest conservative intersection.
Compare target-gene expression in the direct DNMT3L perturbation RNA-seq datasets.

Count target-gene kmer evidence in GSE31454 Tc1/Tc0 brain bowtie files.  GSE31454 provides collapsed read alignments rather than a modern gene-count matrix. The first field encodes a read-sequence count, e.g. ``1_3:1773:50``. This script uses the read sequence column directly and counts conservative target-gene kmers from GENCODE transcript FASTAs.  This is a first-pass target screen, not a replacement for full re-alignment and gene-level quantification.

Download BrainSpan metadata and extract target-gene RNA-seq RPKM values.  The Allen BrainSpan expression service can be fragile, but each specimen has a well-known gene-level RNA-seq file. This script streams those files and keeps only the target genes from config/target_genes.tsv.

Download Allen Institute ISH metadata and quantified target-gene expression.  This intentionally avoids downloading full-resolution image stacks. It keeps experiment metadata, section image IDs/URLs, and StructureUnionize rows containing expression density, intensity, and energy by anatomical structure.

Prepare HOMER inputs for DS/control brain methylation contrasts.  This is a first-pass, array-based DS methylation motif workflow.  It computes context-specific DS-control delta beta values, writes effect-size DMC tables, clusters nearby same-direction DMCs into DMR-like regions, and emits HOMER foreground/background BEDs plus a command manifest.
Prepare GSE305146 recurrent scATAC peak-call sets for HOMER motif enrichment.

Prepare HOMER motif-enrichment inputs for DNMT3L-sensitive methylation loci.  The script makes foreground BEDs for differential CpGs and DMRs, split by methylation direction, and matched assay-background BEDs from all measured CpGs. The resulting command manifest can be run with HOMER's findMotifsGenome.pl to identify known TFBS motifs and de novo motifs.

Scan candidate-linked altered regions for HOMER motif instances.  This is a tighter follow-up to the context-level HOMER enrichment analysis. It uses candidate-linked DMRs/probes/ATAC peaks as foreground regions and scans them with motif files selected from existing HOMER enrichment outputs.  Important interpretation rule: an instance hit is sequence-level motif compatibility. It is not TF binding, and unsupported STAT motif scans are kept as negative-control/exploratory rows rather than enrichment evidence.

Extract target-gene expression from an Allen ABC H5AD matrix.  This script intentionally uses h5py directly so it can run without anndata or scanpy. It reads only the requested target gene columns from sparse H5AD matrices and writes compact per-cell and grouped summaries.

Summarize Allen Brain Cell Atlas manifest files for this project.  The ABC matrices are often multi-GB H5AD files. This script inventories the release manifest, highlights project-relevant datasets, and checks whether the target genes are present in small gene metadata tables that have been downloaded.
